```{r data prep, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# Match map SECTION_NA to report filenames that used "_" for spaces/hyphens
# and dropped periods (e.g. "St." -> "St").
normalize_section_key <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  x <- gsub("[._-]+", " ", x)
  x <- gsub("\\s+", " ", x)
  trimws(x)
}

shp <- st_read("inputs/sections_2025.shp", quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_transform(5070) |>
  arrange(SECTION_NA) |>
  filter(!grepl("water", SECTION_NA, ignore.case = TRUE))

report_files <- list.files(
  "reports",
  pattern = "\\.html$",
  full.names = FALSE
)

reports <- tibble(
  section_key = report_files |>
    tools::file_path_sans_ext() |>
    normalize_section_key(),
  path = file.path("reports", report_files)
)

# Guard against ambiguous matches after normalization
stopifnot(!any(duplicated(reports$section_key)))

shp <- shp |>
  mutate(section_key = normalize_section_key(SECTION_NA)) |>
  left_join(reports, by = "section_key") |>
  mutate(
    has_report = !is.na(path),
    onclick = ifelse(
      has_report,
      paste0("window.open(\"./", path, "\",\"_blank\");"),
      "alert(\"No report available yet for this section.\");"
    ),
    tooltip = paste0(
      "<b>", SECTION_NA, "</b>",
      ifelse(has_report, "<br><i>Click to open report</i>", "<br><i>No report yet</i>")
    )
  )

stopifnot(all(shp$has_report))

states_map <- tigris::states(cb = TRUE, progress_bar = FALSE) |>
  st_as_sf() |>
  st_transform(5070) |>
  st_filter(shp, .predicate = st_intersects)
```

# The Map {orientation="columns" scrolling="false"}

## Column {width=70%}



```{r clickable map, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
map_plot <- ggplot() +
  
geom_sf(
  data = states_map,
  fill = "#285C4D",
  color = "black",
  linewidth = 0.3) +
  
  
geom_sf_interactive(
  data = shp,
  aes(tooltip = tooltip, onclick = onclick),
  fill = "#78BE20",
  color = "#78BE20",
  linewidth = 0.15,
  alpha = 0.10) +
  
  coord_sf(crs = 5070, expand = TRUE) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#f0f2f5", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#f0f2f5", color = NA),
    plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
  )

map_widget <- girafe(
  ggobj = map_plot,
  width_svg = 14,
  height_svg = 9
) |>
  girafe_options(
    opts_zoom(min = 0.5, max = 10),
    opts_toolbar(position = "topright"),
    opts_hover(css = "stroke:#ffffff;stroke-width:2;cursor:pointer;"),
    opts_hover_inv(css = "fill-opacity:0.35;"),
    opts_selection(type = "none"),
    opts_sizing(rescale = TRUE)
  )

map_widget$sizingPolicy$browser$fill <- TRUE
map_widget$sizingPolicy$browser$padding <- 0
map_widget$sizingPolicy$knitr$figure <- FALSE
map_widget$sizingPolicy$knitr$defaultWidth <- "100%"

map_widget
```

## Column {width=30%}

<h3>Landscape information to support FSC US FSS Criterion 6.5 assessments and RSA designation decisions</h3>

This tool helps FSC US forest management certificate holders assess whether native ecosystems are adequately represented and protected in the landscape surrounding their management unit. Use the reports with local information to decide whether Representative Sample Areas (RSAs) are needed under Criterion 6.5 of the [FSC US Forest Stewardship Standard V2.0](https://connect.fsc.org/document-centre/documents/resource/242){target="_blank"} (US FSS).

Select the Ecological Section containing your management unit to open its report. If your management unit crosses section boundaries, review each relevant report.

<h3>What the reports show</h3>

Each report helps you understand:

* **Historical native ecosystems:** The native ecosystems expected under pre-colonization disturbance patterns, given current climate, soils, and other physical conditions.
* **Existing ecosystems:** The ecosystems currently mapped in the landscape.
* **Protection of existing ecosystems:** How much of each existing ecosystem occurs within protected areas and the level of protection those areas provide.

Use this information with local knowledge and other available information to assess whether native ecosystems are adequately represented and protected in your landscape.

<h3>What the tool does not determine</h3>
The reports provide landscape context. They do not identify RSA boundaries, determine whether protection is adequate, or establish conformance with Criterion 6.5.

Local data, finer-scale analysis, field observations, or expert consultation may be needed to complete your assessment. Small or rare ecosystems require particular attention because landscape data may not capture them reliably.


See Criterion 6.5 in the [US FSS](https://connect.fsc.org/document-centre/documents/resource/242){target="_blank"} for the requirements, and Annex G for further guidance.

<br>

# Resources  {orientation="columns" scrolling="false"}

Learn about and download the revised Forest Stewardship Standard for the US at [https://us.fsc.org/forest-management/revised-fscr-us-forest-stewardship-standard-v2](https://us.fsc.org/forest-management/revised-fscr-us-forest-stewardship-standard-v2).

<h2>LANDFIRE Products Used</h2>

* [Biophysical Settings Spatial Data](https://landfire.gov/vegetation/bps): BpS data represents the vegetation that may have been dominant on the landscape prior to European colonization of North America and is based on both the current biophysical environment and an approximation of the historical disturbance regime
* [Reference Conditions Table](https://landfire.gov/vegetation/bps-models): Reference Conditions table is a tool used to describe the historical conditions of ecosystems, including vegetation types, fire regimes, and ecological processes
* [Existing Vegetation Type](https://landfire.gov/vegetation/evt): Existing Vegetation Type (EVT) - represents the current distribution of the terrestrial ecological systems classification, developed by NatureServe for the western hemisphere.
* [Succession Classes](https://landfire.gov/vegetation/sclass): Succession Class data categorizes current vegetation composition and structure into different successional classes based on the Biophysical Settings model.

<h2>Other Inputs</h2>

* [Ecological Sections Data (USDA Forest Service)](https://data.fs.usda.gov/geodata/edw/datasets.php?xmlKeyword=sections).  Ecological polygons used in dashboard to stratify the coterminous US for analysys and report generation.  Formal citation: USDA Forest Service, 2025. EcoMap 2025: Ecological Sections and Subsections for the Conterminous United States. Washington, DC: US Department of Agriculture, Forest Service, Natural Resources and Geospatial Office. 
* [US Geological Survey Protected Areas Database](https://www.usgs.gov/programs/gap-analysis-project/science/pad-us-data-overview).  Data used to quantify levels of protection per Existing Ecosystem within each Ecological Section.
